**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), preferred-level redline to Section 13.4.1.**

- **What's there:** Section 13.4.1 (p0648) is a fully mutual assignment clause — consent required, not to be unreasonably withheld/conditioned/delayed, with a mutual no-consent carve-out for assignments to an Affiliate or to a successor of the relevant business.
- **Why it fails:** Our affiliate/successor rights are fine, but the carve-out equally lets Harpoon assign to its Affiliate or to any successor without our consent, and there is no bar on assignment to a Competitor. That misses preferred elements 3 and 5, and the retained mutual no-consent affiliate exception also means the fallback ("other assignments require consent") is not met. Fallback would only be reachable by deleting our own affiliate right, so I targeted preferred.
- **Change:** One surgical replace narrowing the proviso to AbbVie, barring Harpoon assignment to a Competitor, and confirming a Change in Control of AbbVie gives Harpoon no termination right. The existing "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" standard is left verbatim (mapped as already met), as are the affiliate-responsibility, void-assignment and successor-binding sentences.
- **Not flagged:** Section 13.2 (Change in Control of Harpoon — notice, JGC disbandment, Competing Product handling) runs in our favour and Article 12 gives Harpoon no change-of-control exit, so nothing further was disturbed.
